    How to Report Descriptive Statistics From SPSS in an Assignment

    A practical guide to choosing, reading and writing descriptive statistics from SPSS without copying raw output into your assignment.

    descriptive statistics SPSSmean and standard deviationSPSS resultsdescriptive analysisdissertation results

    Quick Answer

    How should you report descriptive statistics from SPSS?

    Choose statistics that match the variable type, report frequencies and percentages for categories, and use appropriate measures of centre and spread for numeric variables. Present important values in a clean table or sentence and explain what they describe without claiming statistical significance.

    What Descriptive Statistics Actually Tell You

    Descriptive statistics summarise the sample or dataset you observed. They answer questions such as how many respondents belonged to each category, what the average score was, how spread out scores were and what the minimum and maximum values looked like.

    They do not, by themselves, test whether a relationship or difference is statistically significant. Keep description separate from inference. A higher mean in one group does not automatically mean the groups differ statistically.

    Choose Statistics That Match the Variable

    Variable typeCommon summariesExample
    Nominal categoryFrequency and percentageProgramme, employment status, study mode
    Ordinal categoryFrequency, percentage, median where meaningfulOrdered satisfaction level
    Continuous or scaleMean and standard deviation when suitable; median and range or IQR where usefulAge, total scale score, income
    Binary variableCount and percentage for each categoryYes/No response

    Your methodology and data distribution should guide the final choice. Do not use the mean for every variable simply because SPSS can calculate it.

    If you need help preparing or checking your statistical analysis, Academia Helper can provide professional academic support tailored to your research questions, dataset and university requirements.

    How to Obtain Descriptive Statistics in SPSS

    1

    Use Frequencies for categories

    Request counts and percentages and check for unexpected codes.

    2

    Use Descriptives or Explore for numeric variables

    Request measures such as mean, standard deviation, minimum and maximum.

    3

    Inspect the number of valid cases

    Confirm missing values have not reduced the sample unexpectedly.

    4

    Check the distribution

    Review histograms, boxplots or additional statistics if the shape of the data matters.

    5

    Export only what you need

    Create a clean table rather than pasting the full SPSS output viewer into the assignment.

    How to Write Mean and Standard Deviation

    The mean describes the arithmetic average, while the standard deviation shows how widely scores tend to vary around that mean. A results sentence should name the variable and present both values clearly. For example: “Participants reported an average motivation score of M = 3.72, SD = 0.64.”

    Do not interpret a standard deviation as a percentage. Also avoid writing that a mean proves respondents “agreed strongly” unless the scale anchors and interpretation justify that wording.

    For expert SPSS support, data analysis and professionally written academic work, Academia Helper is here to help you turn statistical output into a clearer and better-structured submission.

    How to Report Frequencies and Percentages

    For demographic and categorical variables, percentages are usually easier to read when shown beside counts. A sentence might state that 68 respondents (56.7%) were undergraduate students. If the category table is long, present it once in a formatted table and summarise only the most relevant patterns in text.

    Check the denominator. If some respondents skipped the question, the valid percentage may differ from the percentage based on the total sample. State your approach consistently.

    Create a Clean Descriptive Statistics Table

    VariablenMeanSDMinimumMaximum
    Study engagement1203.480.711.404.90
    Academic confidence1183.760.631.805.00
    Weekly study hours11512.66.4232

    This table is an illustrative formatting example, not research data. Use your actual SPSS results and the precision required by your course or style guide. Avoid unnecessary decimal places and keep the same number of decimal places within a column where practical.

    If you want an experienced academic writer to review your analysis, tables or results section, Academia Helper offers professional support for dissertations, reports and other university assignments.

    Move From Output to a Results Paragraph

    Start with the sample characteristics or variables most relevant to the research question. Report key numbers, then provide a short factual interpretation. Do not repeat every table value in prose. The text should direct the reader to important patterns while the table holds detailed statistics.

    If you later run correlations, regressions or group comparisons, use descriptive statistics as context. Keep causal language out of the descriptive section because no causal test has been performed.

    Common Descriptive Statistics Mistakes

    • Pasting raw SPSS output directly into the assignment.
    • Using mean and standard deviation for every variable regardless of measurement level.
    • Reporting percentages without checking missing responses.
    • Repeating every table value in the paragraph below it.
    • Using too many decimal places.
    • Calling a descriptive difference statistically significant without an inferential test.

    Key Takeaways

    • Match each descriptive statistic to the type of variable.
    • Use counts and percentages for categorical data.
    • Report mean and standard deviation together when suitable.
    • Check valid n when missing data are present.
    • Build clean assignment-ready tables instead of pasting SPSS output.
    • Describe observed patterns without claiming significance or causation.

    Frequently Asked Questions

    Should I report mean or median?
    It depends on the variable and distribution. The mean is common for suitable continuous or scale data, while the median can be more informative for skewed distributions or ordered data.
    How many decimal places should I use?
    Follow your required style guide and use consistent precision. Two decimal places are common for many statistics, but not a universal rule.
    Do I need both frequencies and percentages?
    For categorical variables, reporting both is usually helpful because readers can see the actual count and its proportion of the sample.
    Can I paste an SPSS table into my dissertation?
    It is usually better to recreate useful values in a clean table that follows your university or referencing style rather than using raw SPSS formatting.
    What does standard deviation mean?
    It describes the spread of observations around the mean. A larger standard deviation generally indicates greater variability in scores.
    Should descriptive statistics go before regression or correlation?
    Usually yes. They provide context about the sample and variables before inferential analyses, although chapter structure can vary.
